summary: Forgotten Space Heroes is a seven-slide illustrated story for space enthusiasts aged 9-13. An Apollo Moon buggy, Spirit and Opportunity become fictional narrators, introducing the equipment left on the Moon and Mars and the discoveries it made possible. Short, accessible explanations connect each machine to real NASA mission records, while a final explorer activity invites readers to recall what they learned. The finished project is a self-contained digital storybook, available as a PDF with an editable presentation.
details:
Forgotten Space Heroes is a seven-slide illustrated digital storybook for space enthusiasts aged 9-13. It introduces three pieces of NASA equipment left on the Moon and Mars: the Apollo 17 Lunar Roving Vehicle, Spirit and Opportunity.

I created this project as an individual participant, using AI assistance. Each machine tells its story through fictional first-person narration based on NASA records. Readers discover what the equipment did, why its journey ended and what scientists learned from it. The presentation concludes with a short matching activity and a question about solar energy.

My goal is to make space exploration history accessible and memorable, encouraging curiosity about engineering and planetary science. The creative approach gives silent machines a voice while clearly distinguishing imagined narration from factual information.

NASA mission pages and the lunar artifact catalogue provided the historical and scientific information. Python was used to generate the PDF and editable PowerPoint presentation. ChatGPT assisted with research synthesis, English text, slide layout and code-generated schematic illustrations.

I focused on age-appropriate language, scientific accuracy, readability and source transparency. References are numbered throughout the presentation and linked on the final slide. Illustrations are simplified and not to scale. The project can be read independently or used as a classroom discussion resource.
